biography.plain_text: Sheldon Adelson was an American billionaire entrepreneur who founded and controlled Las Vegas Sands. Raised in a Boston tenement, he made an early fortune through the COMDEX computer trade show and reinvested its proceeds in casinos. He developed convention-led integrated resorts into a global gambling and hospitality business spanning the United States and Asia.

long_biography.plain_text:
Las Vegas Sands reflected Sheldon Adelson's conviction that casinos could use conventions, shopping and entertainment to draw guests beyond the gaming floor. After acquiring the Sands Hotel, he built a privately owned convention centre and replaced the ageing resort with The Venetian, pairing suites with meeting space, restaurants and retail.

Macao and Singapore became the model's next markets, supporting large resorts that Adelson believed could eclipse Las Vegas. The financial crisis brought the expansion programme close to failure, but he supplied fresh capital and kept construction moving. Marina Bay Sands and the Cotai resorts ultimately made Asian operations central to the company he chaired until his death in 2021.
